utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we continue with the -- with hearing the evidence of Mr. Micic, I'd like to ask the parties the following, and it is in relation to the Stanisic Defence. It's Stanisic Defence's request to have an opportunity to address the Chamber regarding the timing of the filing of final briefs. An opportunity to address the Chamber will be given. For us, the problem at this moment is whether we should give you an opportunity to make oral submission or written submissions. The schedule for this week is very tight, although we do not know exactly how tight it is. That depends on how much time the Prosecution would need for Mr. Novakovic. Could we have an impression of that?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it's approximately an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: An hour and a half. How much time would the Simatovic Defence still need for Mr. Micic?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that I may finish by the end of the first session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we hear how much time the Prosecution and the Stanisic Defence would need for the cross-examination of Mr. Micic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We're not anticipating more than 20 minutes, maybe even less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Twenty minutes. Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, my initial estimate is up to three hours, but obviously I'll try to keep it shorter than that if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which would mean that you'd need another hour most likely, one session tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we would have at least the second session tomorrow for Mr. Novakovic. So this is a chance that we would have some time available on Thursday, although it requires the parties to behave very disciplined, because the Chamber is not taking the risk that we would not finish with Mr. Novakovic this week in order to give you an opportunity to make oral submissions. So I leave it to a great extent to you. If you think that there would be sufficient time, the Chamber is quite willing to hear the oral submissions on the matter, but only after the testimony of Mr. Novakovic is concluded. If you think that you could make that and it's a matter of discussing it between parties, then you're invited to make oral -- to make written submissions. Is that clear? Then finally, I do understand that this was a matter the Prosecution wanted to raise at this moment as well, or perhaps not the timing but to -- to make submissions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we were ready. But we're in your hands as to the timing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And, well, you now know what has priority on our minds. Then the parties have sent by e-mail short submissions, as they were invited to do, in relation to the chart which was marked for identification, P3164. The parties are invited to file these e-mail submissions in perhaps the same format, and these are the e-mail submissions 25th of May by the Prosecution and the 28th of May by the Defence. So therefore we'd like to receive it formally filed. If there's no other -- no other matter at this moment, could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Micic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony. And you'll now be further examined by the Simatovic defence. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon to all in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Micic. Mr. Micic, last week we concluded part of the examination. The topic that I'd like us to discuss now has to do with 1993. So sometime in mid-1993, what was the position that you held and where was it that you worked?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In mid-1993, I was still an operative in the AOS. On the 14th of November - I remember that because that's my birthday - I became head of the AOS division.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Micic, so in August you were still an operative in the AOS.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please take a look at a Prosecution exhibit, that is, P2414. It is under seal. So, Your Honours, may it not be displayed to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, we're waiting for the English translation as well. Could you please take a look at the first page, and later on we'll go back to one of the paragraphs on this first page. Can we now please take a look at the second page. Could you tell me whether you recognise the document, and can you tell me whether this is your signature underneath where it says "Operative Radivoje Micic"?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is my signature. Which means that practically I coauthored this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now please move on to the first page again. This is a document dated the 31st of August, 1993, and it is entitled "Official Report on Intelligence about Dafina Milanovic."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may we now move into private session. I would like to mention a name. And then after mentioning that name we can go back into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, in the second paragraph -- or, rather, in the first paragraph, let's deal with that first, you say from our operative source, and then you say further on in the second paragraph: It is interesting that Gerasimovic, the judge working on the murder case - the murder took place on the premises of Dafiment Banka - gave Dafina Milanovic for her birthday a precious diamond of great numismatic value. This information, if I'm not mistaken, you got that from one of your operative posts. Did you check it, though?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. These allegations or, rather, this information was not correct as far as the diamond itself was concerned, or brilliant. Judge Gerasimovic was an investigating judge at that time. On the basis of what we knew about his property and his revenue, this would be nonsense. I can put it that way. Or inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we now please go back into public session. I think that further on ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May we turn into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, let us now look at page 2 of this official report. Last paragraph. This is what it says here: "... D. Milanovic, during the period in question, pointed out several times that she did not trust Frenki because he had promised a lot but failed to deliver on anything, and concluded that Frenki did not trust her either. She said that this was not fair because she, allegedly, at one point in time imported two trucks with equipment, helmets, bullet-proof vests, and night sights from Austria and two aircraft from the United States for Frenki's requirements and, in fact, had equipped 5.000 of his men." So, Mr. Micic, as for this information that you received from your operatives, did you check it any further?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At any rate, like most of the information that can be verified, we checked this too. However, this information itself indicates that it is incorrect. Basically this is impossible. Two aircraft from America, at that time, the end of 1993, quite simply that was impossible. It was impossible to deliver that or import that. There was no way of receiving that in Serbia. Equipping 5.000, men, that's an army. That is an unbelievably large number. As for the question of trust, who trusted who, now, whether it's Mr. Franko Simatovic or Dafina Milanovic, I think that it's a very well-known thing who Dafina Milanovic is -- or, actually, I don't know to what extent the Trial Chamber knows about Dafina Milanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Micic. Just one more question that I'd like to add to this. In 1992 or in 1993 was it possible to import equipment from Austria for 5.000 men without having this registered somewhere and so on?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's put it the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Foundation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Objection: Foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you lay a foundation for your --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness was an operative at that point in time, and he received some information from a source and he checked that. My question is whether in that check -- I mean, the witness already told us that he had not come across anything that was similar to this. However, in view of his knowledge as an operative, he can tell us whether that was possible in the first place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, if there's an objection against foundation, then your -- and when I invite you to lay that foundation, it's not for you to give that foundation but for the witness. To ask the witness such questions that the foundation is laid by him for his knowledge. And the question was -- the question was whether in 1992 or 1993 it was possible to import equipment from Austria for 5.000 men without having this registered somewhere. Is that at least ... if it was at that moment that you intervened, Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: That's precisely the issue, how the witness knows --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: -- what was possible or not and in terms of importing weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Bakrac, so you're supposed, then, to put questions to the witness so that the witness provides the foundation, not that you tell us why you think the witness could tell us what he did. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In your group AOS -- you also said there was another group, a European group. During your operative work, did you check the arrival of foreign nationals, weapons, equipment into the territory of Serbia? Did you have this kind of insight?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly the arrival of foreign nationals at every point in time, whereas the arrival of weaponry, especially this many, this certainly would have been registered by our colleagues from the public security and they would have passed that knowledge on to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you remember that in 1992 at one point an embargo was imposed on the import of weaponry into Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the reason why I said that at that point in time it was impossible. Again, I'm saying that I think that it is impossible. If this had to do with Austria, then three countries would have to be crossed in order for this weaponry to reach Serbia or the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia at the time unobserved. This is an operation that I cannot even imagine.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, Mr. Micic, finally, tell me, when you have some intelligence received from some of your operatives, do you sometimes make remarks at the end of a text?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a integral part of the role of an operative. That is to say, after presenting information or intelligence received from our contacts, we give an opinion of our own. We state what our own position is with regard to this kind of intelligence. However, that seems to be missing here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: That's precisely what I wanted to ask about. Why is there no remark here?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can only go back once again to what I've already stated, that is to say that this -- well, to put it very simply, this is simply impossible. There was no additional knowledge, say, from the public security department or any other security organ in Serbia that would make this possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Otherwise, would you have written something in your remark regarding the reliability of the source?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if this could have been correct information or if it had indicated that the original information has some basis in reality, I would say that it is necessary to take further action with regard to shedding more light on the circumstances involved. I can assume who the source was. It's not right. The source comes from criminal circles, circles closed to Ms. Dafina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, at some point in 1993 or 1994, did you ask to be transferred from the Belgrade headquarters? And if you did, where?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say at what time it happened exactly, end 1993 or early 1994, but I did go to see the then-deputy head of administration, asking him to find me a position somewhere, never mind what kind of duties it involved, that would take me away from the Belgrade headquarters. And the reason was -- this is not a nice thing to say, but the relationship I had with the then-head of Belgrade centre was intolerable.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say "head," you meant the head until that time or the one who arrived in 1993?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The latter.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Whom did you approach with the request to get you a transfer?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean name?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We can go into private session here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You can tell us the name of the person from whom you requested the transfer.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was deputy head of the 2nd Administration, Dragan Filipovic, whom I knew from working together in the American group. And do you still want me to tell you with whom I had this intolerable relationship? That was Zoran Mijatovic who had returned from the 2nd Administration, from the position of head of the administration to the position of head of the Belgrade centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, if you do not mind, I'd like to go back briefly to the -- to the document we had last on our screen. You said it was so obvious that it was -- could not be true, that you did not make any remark about that. Now, is it your evidence that all of what was said by this source was untrue under all circumstances, or is it just the last paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I stress the prefix regarding Mrs. Milanovic, especially the initial information coming from a source that belonged in criminal circles that involved a lot of fraud and dishonest actions. There is not only this reference to a diamond, but you see there is information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please listen to my question: Is it your evidence that whatever is said here by this source is untrue? For example, who attended the birthday celebration of Dafina Milanovic, is that true or not true? Could it be true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose it's possible. I suppose it's true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because you said there's no reason to make any observation, because what is untrue is clearly untrue. Now, if you say that may be true, wouldn't it be important then to distinguish between what may be true and might be of interest and what, as you said, is obviously not true? How would the reader know that -- that the diamond is not true but that the people attending the birthday celebration may be true and that perhaps the -- the confidence Mr. Milosevic may have had in John Kennedy, was that true, was that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a very simple principle. We as operatives collect information. If we had no foreknowledge -- and this especially is an area I wasn't involved in directly. I had no foreknowledge about any of these areas. For instance, there is a reference here to two aircraft from America, which is obviously suspicious. Still it doesn't mean that if I brought it to the leadership - and when I say "leadership," I mean the centre where all the information of all the operatives within the centre is collated - it doesn't mean that they would not order further action be taken to verify and supplement this information to take further operative steps. I could not, and it would have been unprofessional of me to include my judgement on matters I did no -- I didn't know enough about. I was not involved in the surveillance of Dafina Milanovic, and I am not even sure that the leadership did not order further action be taken on this, telling an operative to collect more information.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A minute ago you said that you make an observation. If you would -- you were asked by Mr. Bakrac would you have made a comment like this may be true or this may not be true, and then you said well, it's obvious what is not true and therefore there was no need to do that, but that apparently then does not apply to the whole of this document; whereas on other matters your comment is missing on the likelihood of the observations made by your source.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm saying this again. I did not have all the information concerning the reliability of sources and verifiability of intelligence. It's tantamount to giving an unqualified opinion on -- on inaccurate information. Mr. Bakrac asked me about the last paragraph, which is a case in particular because it's absolutely impossible, whereas the other information isn't necessarily implausible. In any case, I suppose the leadership of the centre would have reacted if there was anything controversial in this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the question put to you by Mr. Makrac -- Bakrac was the following: "... finally, tell me, when you have some intelligence received from some of your operatives, do you sometimes make remarks at the end of a text?" And then you said: "That is an integral part of the role of an operative."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, apparently for most of this report you have not made any observations on the likelihood. And then you were asked: "That's precisely what I want to ask about. Why is there no remark here?" And then you said that you had -- "it's simply impossible." "There was no additional knowledge." Mr. Bakrac didn't ask you specifically on the last paragraph but in more general terms, and what I observe is that on none of the other paragraphs there's any comment on whether it could be true or not. Yes, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it may have been my mistake. I did not follow the interpretation. But when I was asking my question, I wasn't asking about operative officers but operative sources. When they received information from operative sources. I'm not claiming that it's exactly the same in the transcript because I didn't check, but the text says "from operative sources."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but it doesn't change the gist of the questions and the answers irrespective of whether this was very accurate. One additional question: How would you know that the judge - I've never heard of him, so I've got no opinion about him in whatever way - how would you know that he couldn't give a diamond or a brilliant or whatever to another person without verification?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that's what I said. This would take time, but searching through the records that we had on certain individuals within the centre, Belgrade itself, it was established that the judge in question did not engage in anything improper, and we had no information that he was involved in anything criminal or in spying or anything. This is what we normally do with regard to everyone who is mentioned in such reports, especially people like Mrs. Dafina. Operative steps would be taken to find out about the financial situation of the person, and he could have offered a gift like this only if he had -- he had engaged in something criminal, because that's not the kind of money you can earn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, what is still unclear: You said, Well, we send that up and of course it would then be verified. So apparently you did not verify it at that moment. You left it without comment. You did not make any verification yourself. Because a minute ago when I asked you about comments on other matters, you said, Well, if we send it in, then perhaps others would do the verification, but now it sounds as if this is whether -- sounds as if this was routine verification done by yourself, which is not fully in line, I think, with what you told me two or three minutes ago. Any comment on this observation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When an operative is writing on something that is not his personal area of work, he avoids making remarks because he's not familiar enough with the issues at hand. But the leadership of the centre, if they are interested, would order the same operative to gather more information using the same source, and I never received such an order. And the operative source involved was never again used for inquiries of this kind. And if I may add, this is information that I received not within my own line of work but picked up by the way, in passing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Are you aware of the existence of any document in which everything you've now told us is put on paper? For example, the information about the background of the judge, or whatever.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not supposed to know this, but I do know that there are files on the lady, Mrs. Dafina, because she was under surveillance very actively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm asking about the existence of a document in which this report is considered saying, for the judge, couldn't be true because he doesn't have sufficient means to buy a diamond or for the others it's to be verified that those people were present at the birthday party. I mean, a document not generally on the background of -- of the lady but on -- on the accuracy of the information contained in this report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not given any tasks to create something like that, and I did not. But I cannot claim with any certainty that nobody else within the Belgrade centre was tasked with further exploring this matter. It's possible, but I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the simple answer is no, you're not aware of any such document. Please proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, you said you asked Mr. Filipovic to transfer you to a different administration. What did he tell you? Were you transferred?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Deputy head of the 2nd Administration took my request under advisement. He did not give me any answer on the spot. He didn't promise anything. And I definitively moved to the 2nd Administration in June 1994, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you joined the 2nd Administration of the RDB of Serbia, what position were you placed in and what responsibilities did it involve?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was independent operative instructor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what that job involved?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That job involved direct operative work but also training and co-ordination, providing training and co-ordination to individual operatives or centres in the territory of Serbia, with the proviso that the administration could not give orders, but the training role was pronounced.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say that the administration could not issue orders, what administration do you mean?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The then-administration did not have the role in which it could give orders. It assumed that capability only in 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say administration, which administration is it?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd Administration. But also all other operative administrations. So it means that an instructor could not order that something should be done in the centres. Maybe you don't quite understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, how many centres of the RDB were there in Serbia, in the territory of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number varied. Fifteen to 17 at the time. Whether it was 15 or 16 at that precise moment, I wouldn't know. The territory also varied. There was restructuring. Some the centres were abolished, some were merged. But I think I could say around 15. I'm not absolutely sure, but I think that the number is around 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You told us that the 2nd Administration could not issue orders. Can you tell us, then, the heads of the centres reported to whom?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The centre heads were responsible for their own work, and they would receive instructions solely from the heads of the State Security Department for the whole of Serbia, or his deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know in 1994 when you arrived in the 2nd Administration and then in 1995 and later who was the deputy head of the State Security Department?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the late Mr. Tepavcevic. He was the deputy head of the security department.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Micic. If this is the closed session, I think we can go back to the open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We return into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, I think you wanted to say something. But if you see a carat next to a name, it means that it is going to be corrected later. You need not worry about that. In June 1994, when you arrived and you assumed your position there, the position of an independent operative instructor in the -- the administration, do you know what was the position of Mr. Frenki Simatovic at the time?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, Franko Simatovic was a special advisor to the head of the State Security Department.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know whether he as a special advisor to the head of the State Security Department had some special authority?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know, and a later practice confirmed this, is that his job involved primarily investigation and development of technical resources, their application. And later on I also was influenced by him in that regard, especially in the IT department, specifically in the analytics department. This entails also communications systems, especially special communications systems, and to speak even more narrowly, special communications between agents.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it possible to say that the framework of all these activities is something that naturally belonged to the 2nd Administration?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think I can assert this based on my own knowledge. The 2nd Administration had many of those things at their disposal. If you look at the activities of the third branch of the 7th Administration, you will see that they certainly had a lot of technical resources at their disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We heard other testimony here, and our time is quite limited here so I'm going to skip some of the subjects, we heard that the 2nd Administration had a special person in charge of analytics, records, and documentation, as well as a branch for special purposes. Could you explain these things, and why was it so in the 2nd Administration?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be very brief, as brief as I can be, yes, it is true because of the specific nature of its work as opposed to the counter-intelligence. They used -- they had a special methodology to access those particular tools, if I may use that word. Within this administration, it was absolutely necessary to have a separate people working on analytics, on IT technology, and on documentary technology.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Does that mean that the 2nd Administration was different in its status from other administrations?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Talking about its status, I have to say that it was absolutely equal to other administrations, operative administrations and other parts. You can see that very clearly if you look at the remuneration. People who worked in the 2nd Administration and outside, it had absolutely exactly the same competencies and authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say that they had the same competencies and authority, are you talking within the 2nd Administration, because my question was: Did they have special authorities compared to people who worked in all other administrations within the State Security Department?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. It was identical. It was only much, much later, in two thousand and something, when people who worked in the 2nd Administration did not have their special status of an authorised official any more. They did not have that particular ID any more. But up to that moment, within the State Security Department and especially within the operative administrations, the 1st, the 2nd, and the 3rd, they were absolutely equal, except, of course, in the subject matter of their work. That was the only important difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Micic. Very briefly: The fact that the 2nd Administration was rather specific and the fact that they needed to have a special analytics department, IT department, and people working on documentary materials, does it mean that they had particular requirements? I'm talking about equipment here. And if yes, what exactly?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. I'll try to give you an example. The counter-intelligence services are the services that use their own resources, the resources within their own state. We, however, were sometimes forced to use resources that were still the resources of our state but they were specifically resources outside of our state in order to protect our interests. So our method of work was very different from the counter-intelligence people. I could say that the craft is the same, however the tools are very different.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you be a bit more specific? What tools? What tools did the 2nd Administration need?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean technical tools?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Anything that you can explain briefly to us in order to be more specifica, to explain what exactly you meant to say.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, to be very brief: When you say human sources, human means, it means that you have to go and establish contact with them outside the territory of your own country. It's something completely different from the case in which you establish contact within the territory of your country. It means that you have to undertake a series of preliminary actions in order to establish a secure contact. If you establish a contact with a foreign citizen within the territory of our country, it means that you go very deep into the territory of your own country. You normally go deeper than it would be strictly necessary in order to establish a secure contact and to protect your own contact. When we talk about the technology, if we talk about the electronic surveillance, it is something that the counter-intelligence people -- I'm not going to say that they don't know about it, but the intelligence administration uses these things far more than others. Then if you have to establish a contact with the live source, so to speak, you can do it -- nowadays they call it Bluetooth. You have a special modem that can zip the files so you can simply carry it in your bag and you don't have to have an actual contact with this other person. You can still transfer information at a distance. The operative official has to undertake a number of operative measures and activities in order to ensure the safety of the contact. I do not know if anything else --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Micic.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just one more thing. This is a rather complex topic. That is -- it is not easy to explain it in just a few minutes. However, if you have any other specific questions --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Micic. Tell me, in June 1994 when you were transferred to the 2nd Administration of the State Security Department, who was giving you your tasks?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe we should move to the private session for a few moments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, in June 1994 when you were transferred to the 2nd Administration, who was giving you your instructions and tasks?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was only the deputy head of the 2nd Administration, because at the time the head of the administration had not been appointed yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you tell us his name?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragan Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: While we are still in closed session, could you tell us briefly whether you had any contacts with Franko Simatovic, and, if so, what kind of contacts? From June 1994 onwards when you were in the 2nd Administration.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the factor that complicated our everyday work. He insisted that we should have more sophisticated technological work, whatever it meant, and I know about that very well. He insisted that the IT technology should be used within the work of the analytics branch of the 2nd Administration, as well as other fields of work which also should have been performed with more technical resources. Our contacts were not frequent, only every now and then, but whenever we did have a contact, it was on the topic of using of the technical resources in our operative and analytical work.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You as an individual, did you attend those meetings or briefings with Mr. Simatovic as an individual, or was there a number of operatives who attended those meetings?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Everybody went. You have to bear in mind that at the time the 2nd Administration did not have a lot of people working in it, probably not more than ten. So as far as I can remember, it was in the meeting room where he would hold what you could call a briefing or maybe instructions on further development. There were some cases when he had to draw things on blackboard, because I have to admit that we did not understand exactly what he wanted us to do and how. I think that

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, when you were in the 2nd Administration, did you ever receive any specific working task from Mr. Franko Simatovic or any specific operative task?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wait a minute. We shouldn't confuse working and operative tasks. Operative tasks, no. The operative tasks were within the exclusive purview of Dragan Filipovic. That is the deputy head. Working tasks, especially those related to the IT technology, that was something that he influenced a lot within the 2nd Administration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I carefully listened to the questions and to the answers. I'm still wondering what exactly the reason is that we went into private session. I mean, is there BIA source? You didn't ask for that BIA operative --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if you're talking about Mr. Filipovic. Well, whether that's an operative or whether that's a person which was mentioned many, many times. Location, specific technical means. I have difficulties in understanding, but please explain yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my expectation was that perhaps something more specific would be mentioned, things that are used in the BIA today in terms of IT and their operative work. So that is why I wanted to deal with these few questions that way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something? Sorry about that, but may I say something now by way of an example?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. We'll just first -- this -- first resolve this matter and then ... Mr. Bakrac, I'm re-reading now all your questions, and I have great difficulties to follow your expectation that technical details of any specific kind would come as an answer. Earlier we had the Bluetooth, now that's common technology everyone uses in his house and in his cars, so ... Would you tell us -- then the heads of the centres reported to whom? That's a not question which would --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'll try. I'll try. I'll try, Your Honour, to deal with that through my next question, and then we can move into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please. What we're concerned about, whether it would reveal any secrets. Now, if everyone uses it now and if at that time it may not have been very interesting -- may have been a very interesting new development, that's not something that could in any way affect the state security of the Republic of Serbia. Steganography, that I'm not familiar with, or is the transcript ... I'm familiar with stenography. I'm not familiar with steganography. Is there any difference between the two?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't want to lead in anyway. I'm going to try to deal with this through the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Just tell me this: When was it that you first came across this concept, this way of operative work?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again I say that this was what Franko Simatovic had wanted and asked for, that we start dealing with this kind of research and development in realtime.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm mindful of the time, Your Honours. I do apologise to you, but with all due respect, I think that 15 or 20 minutes were used by different questions at the very beginning, so could you please be so kind as to give me this time so that I could conclude my examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You get 20 minutes after the break, Mr. Bakrac. We take a break and we'll resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, you've got until 25 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, during 1994 and 1995, did you hear of Operation Pauk, and, if so, what was it that you heard?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about it, and I was made aware of the reasons for starting this operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what that was.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, practically this had been agreed upon at highest state level. As far as I know, it had been signed by Fikret Abdic, the political leader of the then-Western Bosnia, then Martic and Karadzic as well, together with Milosevic, the then-leader of Serbia, with a view to creating and maintaining Western Bosnia as part of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know about the involvement of the 2nd Administration or part of the 2nd Administration in this operation?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I had not been made aware of the true objectives of the operation. However, since I saw Mr. Simatovic directly, as well as the team that went with him, there were three or four big trucks and perhaps four Range Rovers or Land Rovers. I cannot really make a distinction between the two. They had set out, and on the basis of the composition of the team I could assume what that had to do with, namely that the establishment of a post was the main objective.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please tell us first what kind of post was supposed to be established, and secondly, do you know what these trucks and Range Rovers contained?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: The witness has just said that it was on the basis of the composition of the team that he could assume what it had to do with, the establishment of a post, and he's now been asked specifically what kind of post was to be established. We would submit that there's no foundation for that based on his previous answer, that it's just based on an assumption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, we're not primarily interested in assumptions. If the assumption is based on anything, then please try to find out what that is and then we can consider whether we need the assumptions any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, when you say "on the basis of the composition of the team that had set out," can you tell us which team this is? I think that we are in closed session, so you can give us the names, and then we can move into open session.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, as we've already said, the trucks contained equipment. At that time, I did not know what kind of equipment. However, the people who went along to operate the equipment, and that primarily has to do with radio scouts, the late Ranko Tadic. I can give a name; right? Then Nikola Varda and people around them. It is certain that they were involved in this kind of work. And along with them was the team from the 2nd Administration for the special purpose communications, namely Janko Budimir -- or, rather, Janko was his working name. Ranko Levi [phoen], Budimir Milorad, and this practically indicated that there would be radio reconnaissance, and acting in co-ordination with the others, this indicated that a post would be established. So I had not been made aware of the objectives of the operation for the purpose of keeping the conspiracy, but I did see the results of this involvement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we now move into open session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We return into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, do you know anything about the further involvement of Franko Simatovic in Pauk, and also do you know whether Franko Simatovic went to Petrova Gora?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that towards the end of that year from time to time he went to Petrova Gora. At first it was from time to time and for longer stints several times at a weekly level. However, from 1995 it got shorter. It was only a few days and he went less and less often. That is to say, he left the premises of the 2nd Administration less and less often.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said a moment ago, it's reflected in the transcript, too, when you mentioned the team that went there, you said that later on you saw the results of this involvement. Can you explain to us what it was that you meant?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, practically, in addition to the operative involvement in the field, there was a great deal of radio reconnaissance. We obtained the results of this work in the administration itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Micic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please take a look at 1D3436.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: While we're waiting, Mr. Micic, tell me first of all whether you are familiar with this format of information, MUP Republic of Serbia, the 2nd Administration of the RDB, and then the date.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The date is April 1995, so it seems that information is being provided here about a conversation between Fikret Abdic and Milan Martic and some other detail is being provided. I'm interested in the following: On this first page, do you see something that rings a bell? Do you remember receiving this kind of information?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, specifically towards the very end of this page a certain Sandi is mentioned. As far as I know, he cropped up often in the reports that were sent to the 2nd Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you remember -- do you remember -- do you remember whether this information sometimes contained something that had to do with the position of the Republic of Slovenia that had been seceded from Yugoslavia in relation to the existence of the Autonomous Province of Western Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically it had to do with Slovenia's favouring of this status of Western Bosnia. As far as we know on the basis of these documents, Slovenia even wanted to officially recognise Western Bosnia as an autonomous entity.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we please move on to page 2 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm going to look at a particular paragraph now, and I would like to know whether this would jog your memory in terms of this information reaching you. There is a reference to a certain Slaven who is supposed to come and see Abdic. That is paragraph 3. Around 10.00 he will be at the agreed place at the Bosna Hotel in Banja Luka, and it seems that he's coming from Ljubljana, and Stanic says that he informed his republic of the intention of Fikret Abdic to declare a republic in the AP, and he says that this position was welcomed in Slovenia. Does this jog your memory? Is this the kind of information that you received, and was this of interest to the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Information of this kind, well, naturally arrived in the 2nd Administration. At any rate, this was of significance for the Republic of Serbia itself. That is to say, if this political option were to come to fruition, then, well, things would have been completely different in the Balkans. The game would have played out differently, as we say, from a political point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know whether the Prosecution is changing its position with regard to this document. We asked the Republic of Serbia specifically for all these documents. At this point I would like to tender the document because the witness has recognised it, but Mr. Farr, if he still has objections to this, then we're going to wait for the response of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not -- I'm not aware of the Prosecution having an objection to this document previously. This is a document that the OTP received from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's correct. We have lots of such information. And, well, this document is Prosecution number -- I mean, the Prosecution received this document from the Republic of Serbia, but then I would like to tender it. And I would like to thank Mr. Farr, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, this document without any problems would receive number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D3436 will receive number D1116, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1116 is admitted into evidence. Any need to have it under seal, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, out of an abundance of caution, I would like to have it under seal until we've worked things out with the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, the abundance of caution then would be valid five minutes ago as well, so -- but we'll -- it's admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. Correct, Your Honour. You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, my time is running out, so very briefly: Do you know whether anyone from Belgrade or Serbia went with this equipment, and if so, what was the purpose? In addition to these technicians, this team that you've already referred to.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the very beginning I did not say that in addition to the people or experts from the electronic line of work or whatever you wish to call it, there was a team -- I mean, there were these young men, officials from the ATD, the unit for anti-terrorist activity. As always, when it was necessary to secure not only the post itself or the interception centre, but also the transport of the equipment just as this paper says, it was a state secret, strictly confidential.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You mentioned that the JATD also went. Can you tell us from an organisational and functional point of view in the State Security Service what was that?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1993, the minister of the interior established a unit for anti-terrorist activity on the basis of a document he issued himself, and this was an organisational entity within the State Security Department.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know where the premises of the JATD were, where their seat was?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was in Lipovica at the time, but they also had shared premises with the 2nd Administration on the second floor. There was one office made up of two rooms.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, who used it?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an officer called Milenko who was almost permanently present. I was his best man in Croatia, because we were friends. His name was Milenko. And then there was this -- give me a moment. There was Mr. Radonjic who came very seldom, and Krsman was there even more rarely. Krsmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Micic. What was the relationship between the 2nd Administration and the JATD, if there was one?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In functional terms, it was the same relationship as with all other units, primarily in the sense of providing information and intelligence concerning Western Bosnia specifically. It was information about the ability of transports to pass, and as feedback we would get from them some little intelligence from their own observations, but nothing significant.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said, Mr. Micic, they had one office on the same floor as the 2nd Administration. Can you tell us, where was the office of Mr. Simatovic at the time you joined?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an entirely different wing. The opposite direction from the landing, from the 2nd Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I have to show you very quickly two documents and a couple of questions before I conclude. Do you know what Pajzos is, near Ilok?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was also one of the intelligence centres outside the territory of the Republic of Serbia. I say it was a post because apart from radio interception they were involved in other activities and steps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how you know that?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went there twice, the first time when I continued on my way from the Novi Sad centre towards Pajzos. The Novi Sad centre was in charge of providing logistics to that post, and I brought counter-intelligence information that we obtained precisely by radio interception, and it concerned the unauthorised use of radios and other communications by our members. And the second time, I was there when it was necessary to provide briefing and instruction to the team that operated there, radio interceptors, and analysts, and certain operatives. I was to tell them in which directions to -- to work more on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who provided security to this post?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time the members of the said unit were there. At that check-point there were three of them. On the grounds where this house was - it used to be Tito's villa - there were another three of them. But I believe they worked in shifts, so I don't know the real number.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, we shall now look at two more documents, and I'll have a couple of questions on each of them and that will conclude my examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2D2704. I believe this document should be under seal. We received it unredacted on 15 May from the State of Serbia. In its redacted form this document has been seen before here, and it was part of the Prosecution's disclosure regarding the file on certain Zoran Ristovic, and we received this document from Serbia unrevised and complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, look at the top right corner. It says "Ministry of the Interior, State Security Department, ATD unit." The date is 1st February, 1994, and it's a report on the activities in the territory of the RSK Ilok from 15 to 30 of January, 1994. Have you looked at this page?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, please read through this second page as quickly as you can so that I can conclude my examination and then I'll ask you two things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting, but this is unduly leading. If Mr. Bakrac is intending to ask the witness about the contents of this document, there's -- he should see what the witness knows on this topic before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, that's the usual order in examination-in-chief. Would you please stop reading. Put your questions and then we can look at the document if there's any need to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, have you ever seen the document before?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You haven't. Witness, can you tell me, seeing how you used to work in the state security sector, if we go back to page 1, look at the top. It says "ZNRB" [as interpreted] and then followed by initials. Do you recognise the initials?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- those are the initials of Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And what does ZNRDB mean?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means it was sent to the deputy head of the RDB.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, with all your experience of work in the RDB, what the initials of Franko Simatovic meant?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means he familiarised himself with the contents of the document. Then he would initial it and send it on, in this case to the deputy head.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: If the subject of a report were the conduct of people who were guarding Pajzos, would it have been logical for Mr. Franko Simatovic to be informed about that?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in view of the fact that JATD work was very sensitive and all the harm that could come to this radio interception group and if there was any threat to the whole project, he would be informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to draw the attention of the Trial Chamber to the fact that there is some information about this on page 2. I just want to ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you know about the Special Police Unit's presence in the territory of Slavonia, PJP?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From 1991, PJM, later PJP, were constantly present there, and they were under the command of Radovan Stojicic Badza. The purpose was for them to train local police stations so they can continue to operate and do their part of the job. From 1995 they were called PJP, because milicija changed into policija, and at that time Obrad Stevanovic was the head of those units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you know that in -- within PJM units there was a unit called Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not know that there was any separate unit like that. I know that members changed berets. I don't know how and why, but they at different points in time black, red, and blue berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Micic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to tender this document, too, Your Honours. I have only one more document left and one more question related to it and that would be the end of my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Apologies. Just to say we have no objection to the admission of the document just tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2D1704 will receive number D1117, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1117 is admitted into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my last document and my last question, it's a document we also received from Serbia, from the pile of Mr. Micic, and we added it to our 65 ter list. We hope that this will be approved. It's 2D1698.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It is a certificate, Mr. Micic, regarding you, and I want very brief information about it. The date is 20th February 1998, certificate confirming Radivoje Micic from the 2nd Administration attended a specialised workshop with the title "Organising Intelligence Work Abroad," in the period from 19 January to 19 February 1998, and it lists the topics covered by the workshop. Could you tell us briefly: Who organised this, where, and who is the director Dr. Andrija Savic who signed this certificate?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The workshop lasted more than a month. It was organised by Franko Simatovic personally. You can see there the areas covered by the workshop. Andrija Savic was at the time director of the training centre, so he was the person authorised to issue certificates like this, and you don't need my opinion about Mr. Andrija Savic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Micic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I should like to tender this document, which is from the personnel file of Mr. Micic, and this would be the end of my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2D1698 will receive number D1118, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. And it's admitted into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Micic, thank you very much. And thank you, Your Honours, for allowing me this small extension.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before I give an opportunity to cross-examine the witness, I have one -- one question for you, because matters are not perhaps perfectly clear. You looked at the previous document, which was about Pajzos, if you remember well. You read the second page. Perhaps you could have it on the screen again. Now, the question put to you was: "If the subject of a report were the conduct of people who were guarding Pajzos, would it have been logical for Mr. Franko Simatovic to be informed about that?" And then you explained why it would be reasonable. Now, the question was "If the subject of a report were." I think you earlier said that Pajzos was guarded by the anti-terrorist unit. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us where on this document you can see that the anti-terrorist unit was sent there to guard Pajzos? Perhaps we could have it on our screen again. Yes. This document now, whatever page you would like to read, the first one or the second one, where does it say that the anti-terrorist unit is there to guard Pajzos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this document does not contain any explicit description of the main tasks of the unit in this case. As far as I can see, it's more about the problems that the members of the unit were facing in going about their duties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So this document does not refer to guarding Pajzos as one of the tasks with which the anti-terrorist unit was sent there? Because that was the basis of the question, assuming that. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise, but due to time restrictions and because Mr. Farr reacted, I considerably abbreviated my work on this document. You can see on page 1 the stamp of the RDB, unit for anti-terrorist operations, and it says in mid-1993 this unit was disbanded but the image of the Red Berets that was exclusively used in a negative context --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please -- is this still on page 1 you are quoting from or is it on page 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. It's page 2, towards the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'll give you an opportunity to put your question specifically in relation to that relating to page 2. So do not start explaining yourself what -- but ask the witness questions about it. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Micic, we have seen the stamp on the first page. Now, look at this passage which says that -- which says: "In mid-1993, this formation was disbanded, but the image of the Red Berets used exclusively in negative contexts was transferred to a group that remained in Ilok as part of our unit that was present in Ilok to guard the Pajzos and the white house facilities." And the name mentioned is Radoslav Krsmanovic. Do you see a connection here that allows you to say that part of the JATD was providing security there?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we move to page 3?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would first like to hear an answer from the witness unless he has seen enough, and if -- you asked him a question already without asking him to go to page 3, isn't it? So why not first wait for an answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I had not read in great detail this particular passage describing the responsibilities of the unit in that area, in Pajzos and the white house. It does refer explicitly to their specific tasks and probably not only the tasks of the unit but the command as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask -- of course I've seen that guarding Pajzos is mentioned in this document, but I did not gain the impression until now that it was the unit which is at the head of this document but describing their own activities, but, rather, activities from other groups. This formation was, they planned it, transferred to a group that remained in Ilok as a part of -- and then it's a four unit, perhaps our unit. So it sounds as if -- if that's a reference to our unit, that those were the remainders of the earlier Red Berets formations which are described as already starting in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The entire context is subject to interpretation. You can see at the top there is a reference to the PJM of the MUP of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I can ask questions on the basis of my understanding of the document. You can ask questions but not putting your interpretation of the document to the witness. So if you have any specific questions to the witness so as to -- for example, so as to explain the composition of unit and units which are disbanded and reformatted -- reformed in -- later on and where people from those previous units stayed in the area and were called "parts of our unit," which apparently is the remainder of earlier formations, then you can ask the witness questions about it, but you cannot put to the witness what your interpretation of the document is. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Let me just check this translation, because it says "part of our unit" here. Let's move to page 3, please. And I will conclude with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This document is dated 1st February, 1994. Do you know who Dragoslav Krsmanovic was?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's precisely the person that I mentioned as occasionally visiting the offices on the same floor as the 2nd Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And he was affiliated to whom?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The JATD command. I really don't know what his specific duties were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Micic. I don't know if there is any need for -- we will analyse this document in our final brief, and I don't think there is any need to explore it further with this witness, because I don't think he knows any more about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to find out. On page 3 it is reported that the management of the police station knew that more than 20 former members of the unit, and this is a document of early 1994, were residing in the area of Ilok and that a majority of them were engaged in dirty jobs but that out of fear of retaliation the Ilok Police Station prevented the police station from taking any steps against them. Were you aware of any members or former members of the anti-terrorist unit almost, if I read it well, terrorising the Ilok area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apart from this document, I have no other knowledge about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then the line "The easiest way of concealing such inaction was to claim that those were members of the Red Berets enjoying the protection of the Serbian MUP," any comments on that line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I understand the document, it meant that these, let's call them bad guys who had been expelled or had left the JATD in some other way, held themselves out to be -- or misrepresented themselves as the Red Berets, pretending they were under the protection of the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia, which was not true, and this document says indeed that it was a real danger for the whole ministry, for the JATD, and others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about JATD members leaving the unit and engaging in criminal activity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Really. I had no such knowledge then or do I have any now, in that respect, that is. Which is not to say that no such thing ever happened, but I just didn't know about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, having looked a bit closer at the document, also at page 3, you still are of the view that the document doesn't refer in any way to the task why that the JATD was sent to Pajzos to guard the facility?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could all unnecessary microphones please be switched off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had already apologised for misreading or misinterpreting the document, these one or two sentences. I did not read it carefully enough where there is this specific reference to the tasks of member units in that situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, all my questions derived from the way in which you qualified the document, that's if the document is about this, then either you are in a position to clearly say that it is and otherwise it is asking for confusion, and certainly leading in examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour. Your Honour, I do apologise, but especially the second page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, I think that we can move on --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and if there's any further comment, there are other moments where you can express those comments. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No questions. Mr. Farr, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you may proceed. Mr. Micic, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Farr. Mr. Farr is counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. I don't know if this is a convenient time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is a bit early, but if it would be preferred to have the break now, then we'll take the break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll resume at 20 minutes past 5.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, just a brief matter. There's a Prosecution motion to compel disclosure of notes and photographs from the examination of notebooks. Mr. Jordash in his response I think suggested that rather obtain them on a voluntary basis rather than anything else. Now, what's the position of the Prosecution in light of this? Do you want to put your motion on hold or would you still insist? Of course, we have -- my memory tells me that communication with the expert was not always of the quickest kind. At the same time, Mr. Jordash, do you know if the Prosecution would accept, by freezing its motion, your offer, when do you think you could not only have put the questions to the expert, but also when do you think you could report to us when the expert thinks that he could respond to such a request? Because the first part I take it that you can do it tomorrow or the day after tomorrow, if not today, but the --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yesterday. It was done yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was done yesterday. Okay. That's fine. Do you have an indication as to when you think that the expert might find time to respond to your request?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm happy to put as much pressure on as is necessary and I anticipate then I will get a very quick response. I think the -- I don't have to be too careful about upsetting him now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I'll leave that without any comment as to whether there was any reason before to avoid that. But, Mr. Groome --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- under the present circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Under the present circumstances, Mr. Jordash anticipates a quick response, we'll ask that the motion be held in abeyance for the moment and then we'll formulate our position once we see what the response is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then that's how we will proceed. And, Mr. Jordash, the earlier we have news, I think the better it would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr. I apologise to the witness for -- Mr. Micic, for dealing with other matters. You had to wait, but Mr. Farr is now ready to start his cross-examination. Mr. Farr is, as I said before, counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Micic. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
