utterances.text: Can I start off by asking you whether you ever received an award from the JSO, the successor unit to the JATD?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The JSO, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you a few questions about the relationship between the DB of Serbia and the leadership of the Republika Srpska. Are you aware of any employees or officials of the DB of Serbia meeting with Ratko Mladic in the second half of 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Are you aware of any employees or officials of the DB of Serbia meeting with other senior officers of the VRS in the second half of 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be sheer guesswork. I don't have any direct information.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Are you aware of any employees or officials of the DB of Serbia meeting with Tomislav Kovac, the deputy minister of the interior of the RS in the second half of 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I cannot even remember who this person was, the one that you've mentioned, Kovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Are you aware of any employees or officials of the DB of Serbia serving as a co-ordinator of the forces of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia in Bosnia in the second half of 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that function to co-ordinate the work of somebody else's service, no. Co-ordination, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Co-ordination -- my question is about co-ordination of the forces of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia operating in Bosnia. Are you aware of any employee or official of the DB of Serbia carrying out that function, specifically in September or October of 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only confirm the presence of employees of the state security, but as for the 2nd Administration and its employees in the region of Bijeljina ...

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And which employees of the state security can you confirm the presence of in Bosnia in that time in 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether you are referring to specify names. If so, perhaps it would be advisable to move into closed session or deal with it in some other way, because most of these people are still alive. So I really don't know what the practice of this Court is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The mere fact that they are still alive is not a reason to go into private session unless there are any specific concerns about these persons, but in itself if they are still working as BIA operatives, then that would be a reason to go into private session. I do not know whether the persons you have in your mind are still BIA operatives. If so, please tell me so that we can go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One of the persons, yes, is still an active-duty member; and the others, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, could I just request that we get the name of the one person who still is an active member in private session and then return into open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: So, sir, could you start by please giving us just the name of the one person who is still an active employee of BIA. (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And can you tell us his function, please, at that time in 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We called it reproducer, that is to say, he transcribed onto paper that is to say visible media material that needed to be reproduced.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And could we now return to public session, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will return into public session. The other names are not at the present BIA operatives, so you can use their names unless there's any very specific concern. Therefore, we now move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Radenko Novakovic, first of all. I cannot recall the first name of this other person, but his last name is Lukic. Lukas was his nickname. There were two other employees, and I only remember the nickname of one of them, Nesa from Sremska Mitrovica. And the other one is an elderly man. I really cannot remember his name and surname now. I just want to add something. I don't know whether that is what you consider to be co-ordination. Our terminology is "sadejstvo," acting in concert, the two services acting in concert, because co-ordination implies certain powers of an order-issuing nature. In order to co-ordinate, one has to be in a position to order a particular type of conduct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And when you say "acting in concert, the two services acting in concert," just for clarity, which two services are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this specific case it is the service of Republika Srpska that had to be informed about setting up a post of our service in Bijeljina but also about some other actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Are you aware of any co-operation between employees or officials of the DB of Serbia and an intelligence grouped called Tajfun or Sigma?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never heard of Sigma up until now. Tajfun yes, but at a later stage, mostly from the media. If that is relevant. I think that Radovan Karadzic was the target, but I cannot assert anything because this comes from the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: So it's fair to say you never heard of it in 1994 or 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I most certainly hadn't heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Did you ever learn anything about a possible professional relationship between a person named Mijovic and Mr. Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for their direct relations, whatever we call them, I really cannot qualify them in any way because I don't have any information as to whether they were professional or something else, especially because I first heard of Mr. Mijovic in the context of that well-known - I know it is well-known here - celebration in Kula in 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: So you had never heard of Mijovic any time before the celebration in Kula in 1997; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You mentioned Mr. Simatovic's presence in Petrova Gora during Operation Pauk. During your time in the DB, did you ever learn anything about Jovica Stanisic being present in Petrova Gora?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I don't know of Mr. Stanisic being there, but I'm not saying that he wasn't there. I mean, I'm saying I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: During your testimony last Thursday, you talked about Mr. Simatovic's mission to Knin, but you also indicated that he went to Slavonia in 1991, and that's at transcript page 19780. To your knowledge, when was Mr. Simatovic in Slavonia in 1991?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if it is after his return from Kosovo, then very roughly speaking it would be around the middle of that year 1991 and the three or four months that followed. That's when he was in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: My question was actually directed to Slavonia. When to your knowledge was he in Slavonia in 1991?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr, could you assist me? I have still not the numbered transcript of last Thursday and a search on Slavonia doesn't help me. Could you give us another few words so that I can find the relevant place.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I can -- shall I just read the quote from the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but for me it's important that I can look at the context. So you can read it to the witness, then I'll find the words.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. Very good.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, your answer -- well, I'll start with the question. The question was: "Mr. Micic, to the best of your recollection, in 1991, in his operative work, what locations did Franko Simatovic go to?" Your answer was: "Apart from Belgrade, Mr. Franko Simatovic's operative activities took him to Kosovo --" the transcript says, "in the then-RSK, today the Republic of Croatia, more precisely to Knin and Slavonia, and also there was a period, another period, that he spent at Kosovo." And, sir, my question was: When was he in Slavonia, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The quotation that you refer to was the Republic of the Serb Krajina. I wanted to explain what it encompassed, and that's why I mentioned Slavonia. In my view, I mean I saw him a few times -- or, rather, twice, when I mentioned that I was at the place that was called Tito's villa. I cannot remember any more details. I'd have to think about it. That's the point in time when the RPGs were being established. Now, whether they were mobile or stationary -- well, this is the only involvement of his that I know of on that basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And was that in 1991?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. 1991 -- I'm sorry. I'm sorry. To the best of my knowledge, in 1991 -- I mean, it only had to do with the already-mentioned gentleman Mr. Daniel Snedden and taking various measures vis-à-vis him in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. Can we please have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can I ask one question. When you say, "I was at the place that was called Tito's villa," is that Pajzos where you're referring to or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter 6536 on the screen, not to be broadcast. And specifically if we could please have page 8 in B/C/S, which is ERN 0682-2734, and page 8 also in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, this is a decision dated 19 November 1990, but effective as of the 1st of September, 1990, appointing you to a position in the 2nd SDB Administration in Belgrade, specifically the post set out in Article 42, number 19, and my question is: Is it correct that this is a decision appointing you to your position as an operative in the American intelligence section of the Belgrade DB centre?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. May Mr. Stanisic be excused for five minutes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Again, if you want us to stop --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, we can continue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And could we now please have Exhibit P474 on the screen, again not to be broadcast. And in P474, specifically we'll need page 43 of the B/C/S, which is ERN 06112138, and page 2 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And, sir, this is an excerpt from the personnel file of Dragan Filipovic. It's a decision of precisely the same date, 19 November 1990, effective the same date, 1st of September, 1990, appointing Mr. Filipovic to precisely the same point as you, that is, the post in the 2nd Department of the SDB Administration in Belgrade, defined under Article 42, number 19. Do you recall Dragan Filipovic being appointed to the same position as you on the same day in 1990?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't recall that it was on the same day, but he was certainly an employee of that division or section.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can we scroll to the bottom of the page, and particularly the left-hand side of the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In the B/C/S version we see a handwritten notation on the left-hand side at the bottom. Can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I read it, he received it on that day. The date is indicated. And I suppose this is the signature of Mr. Filipovic, meaning that he received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Are you able to recognise his signature?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say for sure, but I think it's his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Last Thursday you said that during your time in the American intelligence service section the number of operative workers varied from four to seven, and that's at transcript page 19777. Do you recall how many operatives there were during 1991?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not absolutely sure, but most probably there were six or seven.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: So does that mean that your immediate team was either seven or eight people, including yourself, Mr. Filipovic, and Mr. Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I meant them too.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that you worked closely with them and knew them well at that time?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you can put it that way. There was certainly, professionally speaking, close co-operation. We were a tight-knit group. But it's also true that the principle of subordination was strictly observed. We knew exactly who the boss was and who the gofers were, people who brought in information, but there were no close private relations. In 1991 I was going through a divorce, and at that time Filipovic had a lot of understanding for my personal situation, and he accommodated me whenever I had to take a leave of absence to appear before the court. I don't know if you can call that closeness.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to move to a later period now, and for that could we please have 65 ter 6536 back on the screen, again not to be broadcast. And specifically I'll need page 3 of the B/C/S, which is ERN 0682-2728, which is page 1 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And, sir, this is a decision dated the 10th of June, 1994, effective as of the 1st of July, 1994, and this decision appoints you to the post from Article 11, number 3, of the book of Rules on Staff Planning in the State Security Department of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And for the Chamber's and Defence's reference, that book of rules is in evidence as D115 and D833.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, according to that book of rules the position defined by Article 11, number 3, is the post of independent operative instructor, which you told us earlier was your position. Can you confirm that this is the decision appointing you to that position?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that should be it, with my signature. That's the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And can we now please have Exhibit P474 back on the screen, again not to be broadcast. And we'll need page 52 in B/C/S, which is ERN 0611-2147, and page 15 in English. And I note for the record at this point that the date at the top of the page in English is incorrect. It should be 11th of October of 1993, as reflected in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, this decision dated 11 October 1993 appoints Dragan Filipovic to the position defined by Article 11, number 2 of the applicable rules, and this position is the deputy chief of administration of the 2nd RDB Administration. You confirmed that Filipovic was in that position at the time you joined the 2nd Administration. If we could scroll to the bottom of the page. Again, my question is: Are you able to identify that as the signature of Dragan Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think -- I think it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Is it accurate to say that Mr. Filipovic was your direct supervisor at the time you joined the 2nd Administration of the DB?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was quite a different person. If you mean who was my immediate superior. It was a different person, the one because of whom I left the centre. Just before my transfer, just before asking for a transfer, I was promoted into chief of division or head of group, and I had received a letter of appointment to that post, but the prospects were glum in my view because of very difficult intrapersonal relationship and that's why I approached the person I told you about to see if he could help.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting. I can see that my question wasn't clear. I meant after you joined the 2nd Administration. From that time on, was Dragan Filipovic your direct supervisor?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was my immediate superior until 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can we please have 65 ter 6536 back on the screen, not to be broadcast. And now we'll need page 14 in the B/C/S, which is 0682-2757. And unfortunately we don't have a translation of this page available yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: But, sir, can I just ask you whether you recognise this as your employee evaluation questionnaire for 1996?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's our evaluation form, and my signature is there to indicate that I have been made aware of my grades.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And we also see Dragan Filipovic's signature; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like on the previous documents. That would be his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And can you please read the three words in Serbian that appear immediately above Mr. Filipovic's signature so we can get a translation.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean. You mean those three lines?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sorry, the words immediately above Mr. Filipovic's signature, indicating his position.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Would you read them out loud, please.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Manager of organisational unit."

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And why did Mr. Filipovic sign your evaluation questionnaire as the manager of organisational unit?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was no one else. He managed, led, the organisational unit at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And would "organisational unit" there refer to the 2nd Administration?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, yes. They meant the 2nd Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can we now please have page 12 in B/C/S, which is ERN 0682-2755, if I'm not mistaken. And that's page 15 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, are you able to recognise this as your employee evaluation questionnaire from 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it bears my signature, then it is it. Just let me add one thing. Neither I nor many other employees thought much of this evaluation. We did not attach to it any special importance.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: If we look at the bottom of the page, here we see that Mr. Simatovic has signed as the manager of your organisational unit; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was a fax, a facsimile, if that matters. Only he could use it, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And why -- why was Mr. Simatovic here indicated as the manager of the organisational unit?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only suppose that it was because my immediate supervisor was absent, Dragan Filipovic. Why he was absent at that time, I can't remember, and I can't remember for how long. I suppose that all these evaluations suddenly landed on somebody's desk and needed to be signed quickly, and I believe that's the main reason why Mr. Franko Simatovic affixed his facsimile. The deficiency of this document is that there is no worth "za" in front of the signature to indicate that he was not the head of that unit, that he was signing on behalf of somebody else. It did happen that I signed for other people, but I always put the word "za" whether it was my superior or my subordinate that I was signing for.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can you tell us why it would be Franko Simatovic's desk in particular that these evaluations would land on when Dragan Filipovic was absent?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was in his capacity as special advisor or assistant head of department that he did this. Mr. Franko Simatovic was named assistant head of department in 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, sorry. There's an important error in the transcript. Could the witness repeat his dilemma on page 59, line 12 and 13. He begins: "I don't know whether it was in" one or the other capacity. So he could name these two positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the course of 1996, Franko Simatovic was moved from the position of special advisor in the RDB of the Republic of Serbia to the position of assistant head of RDB of the Republic of Serbia. It may seem similar, but it's not the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, our position will be that this document tends to show that Mr. Simatovic was at least functioning as the head of the 2nd Administration as early as 1995, or perhaps even earlier. Are you able to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This signature can certainly not corroborate that. I said tongue-in-cheek that he burdened us, but only in a technical sense. Until 1996 he served as special advisor. After that, after he was appointed assistant chief of RDB, he helped the chief of RDB in intelligence matters. So, in addition... by virtue of his line of work or how should I put it, he was also tasked with the 2nd Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I asked you earlier whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that line 9 does not exactly reflect what the witness said, by his line of work and his responsibilities, what he was to the 2nd Administration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, I have to compare my screens, because on the screen to my left line 9 reads: "JUDGE ORIE: Mr. Bakrac." That certainly is correct. You -- the last sentence of your last answer was: "So by virtue of his line of work and responsibilities," and could you then again tell us what you then said. Not to explain, but just to repeat what you then said. He was in charge of ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe I'll get it wrong again, but we don't understand each other perhaps. As special advisor until mid-1996. Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can't tell you what I meant apart from asking you to again give that answer, because Mr. Bakrac thinks that there may be something wrong. Mr. Bakrac, did I put it to the witness in a correct way?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise to you in advance and to the interpreters as well. Perhaps it is due to my poor knowledge of English, but I believe the sense of what the witness said in Serbian is not "in charge" in English. I believe the meaning is -- is different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please -- when you talked about his line of work and responsibilities, what did you then say was his task in relation -- or what was his task as a special advisor? Was he in charge of anything, or did you say something else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As special advisor, his main duty, as I said before, was technical and technological improvement. I mean of our operative technology. And considering that the 2nd Administration was rather different from other administrations in terms of technology and used technology a lot, especially computer technology in analysis and radio and electronic reconnaissance and surveillance, his role was important. I suppose he also had contacts with other administrations, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there for a second. Mr. Bakrac, if the words of the witness would have been translated not as being "in charge of" but "dealing with," would that come closer to what was your understanding of the response?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, Your Honour. You understood the main thing. That was the point I wanted to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll seek a verification of the translation and see whether it was translated in accordance with what the witness said or whether it's -- there are several ways to translate it. We'll seek verification of that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, I asked you earlier whether you had ever received an award from the JSO, and you indicated that you hadn't. Are you aware of Mr. Simatovic or Mr. Filipovic ever having received an award from the JSO?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know about their awards, but I know -- well, I'm sorry about this imprecision, but I know that some knives were being given out of different types. I think that to this day I have a lighter, but it's a zip lighter. It's basically the RDB that awarded these objects as some kind of an award, but this was apart from formal protocols, apart from regulations. It's not that someone was awarded by way of a formal decision, but things were just given to people, but they were totally insignificant from a material point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, I'm sorry, I didn't understand your answer. Are you aware of Mr. Simatovic or Mr. Filipovic ever having received an award from the JSO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I can -- the witness says that he is not aware of awards but about knives and lighters, insignificant. Do you know whether Mr. Simatovic and/or Mr. Filipovic received any such lighters or knives or whatever was given by the RDB to their employees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I can say with certainty is the following: Since both of them were smokers just like I am, they used lighters with an emblem of the department. Now, in formal terms, whether this kind of a reward was followed by a decision within the department, that I really don't know about. But that doesn't mean to say that there weren't any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But let's be practical. The lighters, I do not know what they do with nonsmokers, but the lighters with the emblem of the department, would you buy them at the department shop, or were they given as a kind of appreciation of work done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it wasn't necessary to buy them. Quite simply they were received. I had a lighter like that, too, but it didn't work for very long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, apparently there is a reason to play down the significance of all this where you were not even asked to qualify. The simple question is: Did they received one; yes or no? And was it related to the performance of work or duties? And you similarly, although you were not happy with the quality of the lighter, I do understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I repeat once again. Formalisation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no need to repeat what you've said already a couple of times. If there's anything you'd like to add, please do so. If you want to repeat what you said, there's no need. Mr. Farr will then put his next question to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to return now to Mr. Simatovic's mission to the Krajina in 1991. On Thursday, Mr. Bakrac asked you the following: "Q. Mr. Micic, you said that you knew Franko Simatovic went to Knin along operative lines of work. Do you know specifically what it involved?" Your answer was: "Well, specifically, the Daniel Snedden case, that's to say, Dragan Vasiljkovic, an Australian national. The work on this case called for work outside ... the territory of the Republic of Serbia." And that's page 19789. How did you know, what is the source of your knowledge that this was the purpose of Mr. Simatovic's mission to Knin?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't only Mr. Simatovic that went to Knin in that period. From time to time Dragan Filipovic went, too, but to a lesser extent. And in direct talks this was mentioned several times, what was being done there, because this was a great novelty as far as our work until then was concerned. It was very brief, like classical operative work vis-à-vis the already-mentioned subject. That's the only thing I know, not more than that, because I was never there myself, directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: So is it fair to say that your information about this depends entirely on what Mr. Simatovic, Mr. Filipovic, or others were willing to tell you about it?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can put it that way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And you had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr, we're willing to tell you, I think I've told you, that would be the right way of putting it --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Yes, I take your point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- because we couldn't -- yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And is it also fair to say that you had no reason to check this information, and you did not check this information?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's superfluous to check what your superior, your supervisor, says. Your then-supervisor. At that point I could not envisage anything else that could be done. I didn't know anything then about RPG or anything else. Also, Daniel Snedden constituted a real threat for the relations within the region then in general terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You were also asked on Thursday when in 1991 Mr. Simatovic was in Knin, and you said: "In any case, that was during the summer. I can't be any more precise than that." And that's at page 19781 to 19782. Our position is that you may be mistaken about the timing and that Mr. Simatovic was actually in Knin beginning in the spring of 1991. Are you able to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing more than what I've already stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Is it correct that Mr. Simatovic's mission to the Krajina was undertaken with the permission and knowledge of the leadership of the DB of Serbia, if you're able to say?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can just apply logic. I am justified in assuming that he could not have gone there on his own. He had to get some approval in order to engage in operative activity outside the territory of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And based on your knowledge of how the DB functioned at that time, who would ordinarily have had to provide that approval?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I was an ordinary beginner without any particular high posts. Now, how could I conclude what the minister of the interior would decide on and what the head of the department would decide on, to what extent they could take decisions independently? At any rate, the department was just -- I mean, the department for state security was just a department within the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Now, you've -- you've told us that Mr. Filipovic spent time in Knin at this time as well, and we've seen that you and Mr. Filipovic had the same position. Is it your evidence that you can't tell us who would have given -- who would have had to give you approval to do operative work outside of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am just assuming -- actually, I know what would have been sufficient for me, that is to say that the head of the group or the head of the division would give an order. However, following the formalism of the then-8th Administration, the one that was involved in logistics, legal grounds would have to exist -- or, rather, a decision would have to be made, and other things would have to be taken care of, like the money that would necessarily be spent on such a mission. And as for the technical resources needed, I would deal with the -- I would actually address the office that dealt with that. When I say technical resources, I'm saying that operative work required some special technical resources too. When I say that, I mean if I'm issued with a particular piece of equipment, I have to sign a document saying that I had been issued with that particular piece of equipment. I'm just giving this by way of an example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr, is there any way that we could leave the realm of assumptions, logic, et cetera, and rather go back to the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, in addition to Mr. Simatovic and Mr. Filipovic, there has been evidence in this case that Milan Radonjic was also in Knin at this time. Were you aware that he participated in this mission as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, that's at transcript page 16708.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I had no knowledge about Milan Radonjic because he was in a completely different division. If I'm not mistaken, at that time he was dealing with the subject matter of the Israeli intelligence service, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Now, based on things that you were told about this mission, did you ever hear whether this mission had been approved by authorities in the SAO Krajina as well?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If we are talking about 1991, the details of the arrangement, if I can put it that way, or of the stay there, I really had no knowledge about that, none whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: During the time he was in the Krajina, as far as you know, did Mr. Simatovic prepare any reports on the activities of Daniel Snedden?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of that. I repeat once again: I was not directly involved in working on Daniel Snedden, but if someone looks at the file, then this can either be confirmed or refuted. If I may just take a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, our time is short. I'd prefer to move on. I'd like to turn briefly just to the question of the extent of your knowledge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr. It was not quite clear to me, but when you said, "If I may just take a minute," did you intend to take a minute to explain things further, or was there any other reason for which you needed a minute?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just to give an example why that was the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can you tell me if this is accurate: Because of the principle of conspiracy, in general your DB colleagues would not necessarily tell you about all of their activities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if we understand each other correctly. What do you mean by "conspiracy" as "zavera"? Conspiracy as in "konspirativnost" is one of the main principles for the functioning of any service of this kind in Serbia and outside Serbia anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And is it fair to say that that principle is essentially that even members of the same service should only share information with each other on a need-to-know basis?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That was my example in terms of expressing unauthorised interest for Mr. Daniel Snedden. Two persons left the security service because of that. It was that strict. They were dismissed from the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could you just explain in a bit more detail why they were dismissed?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is this principle of everyone doing the work that he or she is in charge of. If you express unauthorised interest or if you jeopardise in any other way the implementation of missions with regard to a particular subject, you are punished most strictly. In this particular case, I know of two individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And can you tell us who they were and how they expressed interest in this case that led to their dismissal?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean we, all the other employees, were told about that at a separate meeting of the head of the division, but the least possible information was given. At this same meeting I insisted that the punishment be even more severe. It is disclosure of a secret, and that's very serious. I never expressed interest in anybody else's work. I cannot remember the name of one of these individuals, and the other one I see from time to time to this day. So ...

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Could we please have Exhibit P2420 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And, sir, while the document is coming up, I'll tell you that it is an Official Note on the heading of the 2nd Administration of the RDB. It is dated 27 June 1994. So this is just a few days before you joined the 2nd Administration. And if we could have the second page in B/C/S and the bottom of the first page in English. And here at the bottom of the document we see the words "Deputy Chief of Administration, Dragan Filipovic," and below that a signature. Sir, again can you confirm that this is the signature of Dragan Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It should be his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And can we please go back to the top of the first page in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And we see here that the document is entitled "Official Note on the Tajfun Group," and I'll begin reading at the top of the document. It says: "Because of the internal conflict and discord in the RDB and the RJB of the Republic of Serbia, the intelligence group known under the pseudonym Tajfun from Banja Luka, as well as the Banja Luka Department for Narcotics have decided to reduce their intelligence activity since they've started having doubts that their intelligence reports that they have been preparing have not been reaching the right end user (the president of the republic) but, on the contrary, have been ending up in the hands of unknown people. "The members of the Tajfun group have therefore decided to establish contact with the 2nd Administration of the RDB of the Republic of Serbia MUP explaining that we were the only institution they still have faith in and stating their wish to forward their intelligence and information directly to us in the future, and so leaving the processing of intelligence and its distribution to us. "We let the members of this group know that we will accept the group's initiative only under the condition they get approval from the president of the republic, Radovan Karadzic, and the minister for the interior, M. Stanisic. Since the said group informed us that they got Karadzic's and Stanisic's approval, we are of the opinion that this segment of the intelligence bodies of the Republika Srpska should be subsumed under our system."

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And next page in B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: [As read] "The technical aspects of a two-way communication were therefore analysed, and the said group will form now -- will from now on contact us under the pseudonym Sigma. "The preliminary discussions on Sigma's incorporation into the intelligence system of the RDB of the Republic of Serbia MUP were held by the chief of the 2nd Administration of the RDB of the Republic of Serbia MUP, Franko Simatovic, and the Deputy Chief of the 2nd Administration of the RDB, Dragan Filipovic." Now, I asked you earlier today whether you had any knowledge of an intelligence group known as Tajfun or Sigma, and I believe you said you you did not have any knowledge during the period 1994/1995, and that what you know, you know only from later media reports. Is it really your evidence that you had no idea that Franko Simatovic and Dragan Filipovic were making these arrangements with this group?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not only that this is the first time that I see this document or, rather, am made aware of its content. That's one side. And then on the other side, my subsequent work and my work in the 2nd Administration did not even hint at what is mentioned here, except for the part that I've already referred to, the Bijeljina post.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. Could we please have the top of the first page in both languages. And I'm interested in the handwritten remarks at the top, starting on the top left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Now, sir, earlier, when I was reading out the entire text of the letter, I read a portion that included the words "the preliminary discussions on Sigma's incorporation into the intelligence system of the RDB of the Republic of Serbian MUP were held by the chief of the 2nd Administration of the RDB of the Republic of Serbia MUP, Franko Simatovic, and the deputy chief of the second administration of the RDB, Dragan Filipovic." Now, sir, doesn't this show that Mr. Simatovic was in fact functioning as the chief of the 2nd Administration at this time?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already stated in which field my knowledge is in terms of Franko Simatovic's presence in the 2nd Administration. Now, what Fica wrote, I cannot really stand by that. But obviously Franko is suggesting what should be done further, that is to say, to open a file. This is purely analytical work. But the decision was no. Why it was no, that I would not know how to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Now, you indicated also when you were in the 2nd Administration you never received any tasks from -- from Mr. Simatovic. Do you have any knowledge of why Mr. Filipovic appears to be receiving a task from Mr. Simatovic via this handwritten note?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only suppose at that time work with a network of agents was of such a scope that it was not easy to make quick conclusions. I suppose this was rather a request for a professional opinion what should be done next on the case that we just read about, how to use the agents outside the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can we now please have Exhibit P2941 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And, sir, while this is coming up I'll just orient you by telling you that now we're moving to a later period, which is specifically the second half of 1995. And this is specifically a letter dated the 26th of September, 1995, that we'll see on our screens in just a moment. And if we could just zoom in a little bit more on the signature at the bottom, we can see that it's signed in the name of Tomislav Kovac as deputy minister. And if we could zoom out again, we can see that the ministry in question is the Ministry of the Interior of the Republika Srpska. And I'll just read the first -- sorry. In the letter we also see it's addressed to General Ratko Mladic as the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS. And I'll read the first paragraph of the letter. It says: "I propose to schedule a meeting between the RS Deputy Minister of the Interior Tomislav Kovac, the co-ordinator of the forces of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia, Dragan Filipovic, and you to resolve certain problems with regard to the commanding of troops currently under the RS MUP." Now, you told us earlier that you had knowledge of any member of the Serbian DB meeting with either Ratko Mladic or Tomislav Kovac in September or October 1995. Were you even aware that Tomislav Kovac was trying to arrange such a meeting among himself, Dragan Filipovic, and Ratko Mladic in September of 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only repeat what I stated earlier. I would need a lot of time and material to even recall who Tomislav Kovac was. I have no closer or better knowledge. At the time when we first mentioned him, I didn't even know who he was. Should I go on? I would use this formula for a good legend in another country. I would say that I'm a co-ordinator of some special group attached to the Ministry of the Interior to get these people to work for my intelligence service. That's what I would do. Maybe that title existed, but I'm not aware that Dragan Filipovic was any sort of co-ordinator of forces within the MUP. He was my boss, but he was not co-ordinator of forces within the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you the following question: You earlier said, "Unfortunately --" "Unfortunately, when asked about Tomislav Kovac, I cannot even remember who this person was, the one you've mentioned, Kovac." Now, a few lines ago you said: "At the time when I met him, I didn't even know who he was." On the one hand you tell us that you do not know who Mr. Kovac is, and at the same time in your last answer you said you met him, but at that time you didn't know who he was, but there may be an error, because it's -- could you please explain? And if need be, of course, we'll check whether your words are translated and scribed accurately, but that's my problem at this moment, reconciling the two answers you gave as it reaches us -- and they reach us in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry I didn't follow the interpretation, but I'll repeat once again. Neither then nor now until this moment that name told me nothing and doesn't tell me anything now. I just don't know who that person is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What did you then mean when you said: "At the time when I met him, I didn't even know who he was." What's the meaning of that sentence? Can you explain to us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really can't go back to that context. I can't recall it. But it was not -- I couldn't have said anything about meeting Tomislav Kovac. Maybe I should -- maybe you should quote to me what I said before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll read your entire answer. You said, when asked about Tomislav Kovac trying to arrange a meeting among himself, Dragan Filipovic, and Ratko Mladic in September of 1995, your answer was: "I can only repeat what I said earlier. I would need a lot of time and material to recall who Tomislav Kovac was. I have no closer knowledge. At the time when I met him, I didn't even know who he was." That was what your answer -- how it was translated and transcribed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant probably that when I met Filipovic, Dragan, I had no prior knowledge, and I still don't know anything about Tomislav Kovac. He was never a subject of conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I let this pass because I didn't want to suggest anything, because it might be my mistake. I wasn't following the transcript. I did not hear the witness mention meeting Tomislav Kovac. I don't know. Maybe -- I don't know whether it's necessary to check the recording, but it's my mistake. I wasn't following.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it's not your mistake. I would like to know what the witness said, Mr. Bakrac. That's the issue at stake, not on who in time asked for translations or anything else. Madam Registrar, I would like to have those lines verified from the audio, and as far as the translation is concerned, and of course the transcription. Mr. Farr, I would like to read one decision, so therefore I suggest that we adjourn for the day. Are you on time in your schedule?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I estimate another hour and a half, Your Honour, so, yes, I think I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could try to see whether you could do it in one session that would be appreciated. So be as efficient as --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd like to instruct you again that you should not speak or communicate in any other way with anyone about your testimony, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.00 in this same courtroom, and we'll conclude your testimony tomorrow. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to deliver a decision on rebuttal deadlines. The Chamber addresses the Prosecution's request to extend the deadline for rebuttal filings. On the 1st of May of this year, the Chamber instructed the Prosecution to file requests or notification of rebuttal evidence no later than the 8th of May, 2012. With regard to Defence evidence admitted after the 8th of May, the Chamber instructed the Prosecution to file any such motions no later than one week after the date of the introduction of such evidence. You can find this on page 18810 of the transcript. On the 8th of May, the Prosecution filed its notification regarding rebuttal evidence. In its notification, the Prosecution requested the Chamber to adjust the deadline for rebuttal filings in relation to Defence documents which have been tendered and for which a decision on admission is pending. The Prosecution requested that this deadline be set to two weeks following the find decision on admission. The Prosecution noted that the Defence had tendered many Defence documents from the bar table for which a decision on admission was pending and which could potentially trigger additional rebuttal evidence. On the 24th of May, the Prosecution orally requested to adjust the deadline for rebuttal filings in relation to Stanisic Defence bar table documents to seven days from the final decision on admission of such documents by the Chamber. The Stanisic and Simatovic Defence submitted in court that they did not object to this request. The Chamber accepts that the Prosecution will be in a better position to determine if rebuttal evidence, if any, once it has a full overview of the documents, if any, still to be admitted in the Defence case. In view of the scheduling of the remainder of the trial, the Chamber considers that a one-week time period remains appropriate. The Chamber accordingly grants the Prosecution's request in part and sets the deadline for rebuttal filings in relation to documents tendered by the Defence and admitted after the 8th of May, 2012, to one week after the Chamber's last decision admitting documents in the Defence case. In its notification, the Prosecution further requested the Chamber to adjust the deadline for rebuttal filings in relation to the final four Defence witnesses, namely Milosevic, Plahuta, Vujovic, and Micic, to two weeks after the last of these witnesses has finished testifying. The Prosecution requested the same in relation to the re-called Defence witness Novakovic. The Prosecution submitted that these witnesses were all expected to testify about the structure and membership of the Serbian DB. The Prosecution anticipated that it would make inter-related rebuttal submissions in relation to their testimonies. Neither the Stanisic nor the Simatovic Defence responded to this request. On the 21st of May, the Chamber suspended the deadline for rebuttal filings in relation to the aforementioned witnesses, pending the present decision. The Chamber informed the parties accordingly through an informal communication which is hereby put on the record. The Chamber accepts that it may be more efficient for the Prosecution to make rebuttal filings once the four aforementioned final witnesses have testified. The Prosecution should already have a good overview of Witness Novakovic's testimony, who is being re-called for further cross-examination. The Chamber considers that a one-week time period remains appropriate. The Chamber accordingly grants the Prosecution's request in part and sets the deadline for rebuttal filings in relation to witnesses to one week after the last of these witnesses have finished testifying. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. So there is a distinction between Novakovic and the others, but Novakovic is the last one anyway who will appear. We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 30th of May, at 9.00 in the morning in this same courtroom, II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 30th day of May, 2012, at 9.00 a.m.
